studies.title: My Sydney Marathon: lessons from a sub-four attempt
studies.description: I aimed for sub-four at Sydney. Here are my training weeks, late-race splits and the lessons I took home.
studies.insight: My biggest week was 38.1% above my 12-week average. Compare the full build with the marathon time predicted from my half.
studies.question: What did my training miss before Sydney?
available_data: Recorded rehearsal laps and personal recollections
studies.observed: Selected recorded pace slowed from 5:32/km at km 25 to 6:50/km at km 33; recorded heart rate stayed within 160–164 bpm.
studies.limitations: Kilometre 26, the full race trace and official checkpoint comparisons are not available. These observations do not diagnose the cause of the slowdown.
studies.takeaway: Choose a target from repeatable preparation and practise a plan that still works late.

studies.title: My two Run Melbourne half marathons: from fading late to finishing strong
studies.description: I faded in 2025 and finished strongly in 2026. Compare the recorded laps from both Run Melbourne halves.
studies.insight: The later ten laps took 6:08 longer in 2025 and 0:32 less in 2026. The replay shows where my pace changed.
studies.question: How did my two half marathons unfold?
available_data: Displayed heart rate, elevation and activity summaries
studies.observed: The first-to-fourth 5 km block pace changed by +50.8 seconds/km in 2025 and −6.8 seconds/km in 2026.
studies.limitations: The 2025 activity notes GPS distance loss. Recorded kilometres are not matched course positions, and the records do not isolate training, conditions or fueling.
studies.takeaway: Read the broader lap pattern alongside effort and context, rather than treating one fast finish as a marathon guarantee.

studies.title: My marathon fueling experiments: what I learned from homemade and commercial gels
studies.description: Homemade gels felt thick and drying. At Sydney, familiar commercial gels became hard to take too.
studies.insight: My plan was a gel every 20 minutes. Late in the race, taking the next one became the problem.
studies.question: What can I keep eating late in a marathon?
available_data: Personal homemade and commercial gel experiences
studies.observed: The homemade mix felt thick and drying; familiar gels also became unappealing late at Sydney. These are personal observations.
studies.limitations: There is no verified recipe, consistent product-variant record or complete measured race intake. The account is not a controlled product comparison.
studies.takeaway: Record exact servings, planned versus actual consumption, drinks, effort and symptoms before drawing a conclusion.

studies.title: Rebuilding after Sydney: my plan to finish the next marathon stronger
studies.description: The changes I want to make after Sydney: steadier training, controlled workouts and more useful fueling practice.
studies.insight: I want more consistent weeks and better rehearsals. These are my plans for the next build; the results are still to come.
studies.question: How will I prepare for the next marathon?
studies.observed: The previous 12 complete weeks averaged 60.7 km/week; 83.9 km was the peak rather than the normal week.
studies.limitations: The proposed sequence is not a current log, dated programme, rehabilitation schedule or evidence that the rebuild has worked.
studies.takeaway: Plan from routine and response, then judge actual training before escalating the next target.
